body:
## Problem

The dashboard currently mixes several interaction types:

- Tool Source cards/names semantically filter the chart by tool.
- Model Breakdown `Focus chart` buttons semantically filter the chart by model and clear the tool focus.
- Chart legend items visually hide/show series, but do not mean the same thing as filtering.

This feels weird when the same normalized model appears under multiple tools, e.g. `gpt-5.5 (openai)` under OpenCode and Codex CLI. Users can reasonably expect combinations like `Tool: Codex CLI` + `Model: gpt-5.5`, but the current UI toggles between modes instead.

## Proposed solution

Design and implement an explicit filter model for chart/table interactions.

Preferred direction:

- Use visible filter pills, e.g. `Tool: Codex CLI ×` and `Model: gpt-5.5 (openai) ×`.
- Allow tool + model filters to coexist as an intersection where useful.
- Keep legend items as chart-series visibility only.
- Rename or annotate legend/source/model controls so their behavior is obvious before clicking.

## Alternatives to evaluate

1. Global tool filter chips near the range tabs, applied to overview/chart/table/history.
2. Separate chart source focus and Model Breakdown tool tabs.
3. Combined tool + model filter pills across chart and table.
4. Minimal copy-only pass that labels legend controls as show/hide and filter controls as semantic filters.

## Acceptance criteria

- The chosen interaction model is documented in visible UI text.
- Tool filters and model filters do not silently erase each other unless that behavior is explicit.
- Legend controls are visually and textually separate from semantic filters.
- Duplicated model names across tools are handled predictably.
- Browser smoke covers source click, model focus, legend toggle, clear-filter behavior, and no console errors.

Part of #9.
title: Clarify chart filter semantics for tool, model, and legend interactions
